strongest_case: V6 substantially and correctly repairs most of the adjudicated V5 defects without reducing the design. The 132-byte canonical empty base and complete six-node/eleven-edge/two-loop/six-claim replacement repair R02; the fixed-versus-future SK10 binding distinction repairs R03; the audit path/hash versus byte-payload names repair R05; and the isolated SKN06 comparator, candidate blindness, aggregate-only SKE11 declassification, terminal SKN05, and external SK10 are the right architecture for R01. Independent review of the bound construction supports the preserved finite specification: 4!*2!*2!=96 alignments quotient to 48 graphs and six calibration classes of 16; LOCAL and RANDOM_SOURCE have exact value 1/4, MOTIF_SCHEMA and ORACLE have value 1; pi-inverse rendering and GRAPH_012 != GRAPH_016 close the direction ambiguity; tau is involutive and content-changing; costs remain 5/8/16/17; 36,864 typed bridge cases yield 73,728 single-product deletion checks; and the 72-vector and ordered 25-call registries remain narrow governance oracles. The exact three requested and eight forbidden scope atoms are disjoint, the actual transitive ratification chain is used, every C01-C06 claim is non-headline, LOCAL is target-local rather than atoms, MOTIF_SCHEMA is direct complete-graph access rather than learned induction, and no proposal artifact conveys implementation, execution, audit, compute, promotion, benchmark, or scientific authority. The systems interpretation is nevertheless too permissive about exact constructibility. The complete graph calls every edge one-way, gives SKN06 no edge to a candidate, and simultaneously says SKN06 passes call inputs; co-visibility does not supply direction, and the compound negative-registry item hides stimuli candidates must receive together with expectations they must not receive. That is a blocking incomplete R01 repair. SK10 also lacks a non-self-referential request-file grammar: the only schema-defined request object includes the request file's own SHA-256, so either literal construction is circular or the actual file fields are unstated. The direct-AST/static-CLI deterministic subset is also materially underdefined, especially F03/F04 identifier and allowed-write matching, but this is not a security blocker because the already-required fresh human review can conservatively adjudicate those semantics; the smallest honest repair is to make the syntax matcher exact or move its judgment-dependent portion to that review. Sealed oracle transit through SKN01 is a semantic-visibility clarification, not a candidate leak: opaque byte transport and hash verification can coexist with no semantic decoding, or SKN06 can read the hash-bound bytes directly. V6's split audit hash bindings are likewise metadata, not capabilities. These findings preserve SK06-SK07, valid mathematics, exact scopes, terminality, and claim limits while requiring rework only where the bound execution/audit path is not exact.

concerns.statement: V6 adds the correct isolated comparator and candidate-to-comparator observation paths, but its complete directed graph has no comparator-to-candidate invocation/input path; the compound negative fixture item also joins candidate-visible call stimuli to comparator-only expected exceptions.
concerns.evidence: Every SKE edge is called an exact one-way information-flow edge. SKE07, SKE09, and SKE10 point only from candidate surfaces to SKN06, SKE11 points from SKN06 to SKN05, and symbolic_contract.md section 3 expressly says SKN06 passes call inputs while also saying it has no edge to a candidate. Matrix co-visibility of LOCAL/MOTIF/RANDOM/ORACLE input fields says which stages may observe a value but does not define its source or direction, and it contains no projection_id/args_tuple/control item for malformed or wrong-arity calls. The only source of the exact 25 negative stimuli is oracle.negative_registry_25_calls_and_expected_exceptions, which is visible to SKN06 but forbidden wholesale to all candidates. Consequently the graph either relies on undeclared reverse flow or must expose an overbroad compound oracle payload. Without exact invocation, SKN06 cannot derive all claimed observations and SK09 cannot validate their aggregate receipts.

concerns.statement: SK10 cannot construct or verify the promised exact request bytes because the contract points to schema-defined fields, while the schema defines only a receipt request record that includes the request file's own path and SHA-256.
concerns.evidence: audit_contract.md section 3 requires a canonical JCS-plus-one-LF scope_audit.request.json containing exactly the schema-defined fields. scope_audit.schema.json has no standalone request schema; its sole request object is independent_review.request and requires path, sha256, request_id, change_id, three proposal hashes, diff base, manifest root, identities, frozen_at, and created_at. If that object is the file grammar, sha256 must equal the hash of bytes containing itself. If path/sha256 are later receipt metadata, the exact request key set and byte-equality rule are not bound. The receipt can structurally validate while binding an arbitrarily chosen external request, so request_binding and freshness are not exact falsifiers. This is a constructibility defect in required SK10, not a demand for extra security machinery.

concerns.statement: V6 honestly moves complete call/capability/reachability analysis to fresh human review, but the remaining deterministic forbidden-AST/static-CLI partition still lacks an exact reproducible matcher.
concerns.evidence: File discovery, hashing, manifest encoding, Git path equality, Python 3.9 parsing, literal import enumeration, and the declared no-argument CLI can be recomputed exactly. F02-F05 instead use prose such as direct uses/references, direct syntax, syntactic candidate for the sole allowed write, and direct identifier components without binding AST node patterns, qualified-name treatment, token/component splitting, case normalization, string/comment handling, or allowed-write recognition. Two careful reviewers can produce different forbidden_ast_findings while each follows the text. This does not justify a security-proof evaluator and is not independently blocking because section 3 already requires conservative source review and human adjudication; it is a material incomplete R04 partition and deterministic-claim overstatement.

concerns.statement: SKE04's authority-originated sealed copy needs a precise semantic-visibility reading, but opaque transit and public hash metadata do not expose oracle semantics to a candidate and are not independent blockers.
concerns.evidence: The matrix forbids SKN01 semantic visibility to all three oracle payload items while SKE04 says authority forwards an integrity-checked immutable copy whose payload visibility begins only at SKN06. This is coherent if visibility means semantic decoding and SKN01 handles only an opaque byte envelope; otherwise SKN06 can read the context-bound V5 golden_vectors bytes directly after authority release. In either case every candidate remains forbidden expectations. Separately, V6 correctly splits audit.contract_bytes and audit.schema_bytes from audit.contract_sha256_context_binding and audit.schema_sha256_context_binding: SKN01's visibility to paths/digests is necessary binding metadata and confers neither the bytes nor an audit capability. Treating a digest alias as a leak would repeat the security-theater reading rejected by V5 R05.
